definition: Requesting, granting and removing user access and roles in trading and operations systems.

synthesis.description: Desk heads, schedulers and risk staff ask IT or system administrators to add, change or remove users in trading and operations systems such as Sitara, Enpower, RiskTrac, EnronOnline, schedule tools and distribution lists, or to issue trader IDs and passwords. Requests list names and NT usernames; administrators collect access criteria and lists of who should have access per desk, process the request, and confirm by email or automated notice. Around the new company launch, whole desks were set up and verified at once.
steps: A manager or user emails a request naming the people, the system and the access or role needed.
Administrators collect access criteria or a list of who should have access for each region or desk.
The request is entered into the access request system, which notifies approvers.
The administrator creates, changes or removes the accounts, IDs or passwords.
Confirmation goes back to the requester, often with login details or setup instructions.
The requester or desk checks that users can log in and trade, and reports any accounts that failed to set up.
synthesis.approach: Route every access request through one form that captures person, username, system, role and approver, keep a per-desk roster of who should have which access so administrators do not have to ask for lists each time, and run a post-migration check comparing the roster with accounts actually set up.
synthesis.rationale: Requests arrive as free-text emails with names and usernames, and administrators repeatedly ask desks for access lists. A standard request and roster template removes the back-and-forth and gives a list to verify against after system changes.
